text.p: Uganda's main category 91-day T-bills were marginally oversubscribed at this week's auction on Wednesday, the central Bank of Uganda said on Thursday.
The bank said that it sold 5.8995 billion shillings in T-bills in competitive rates and 104.4 million shillings in non-competitive rates. It had offered 6.0 billion for sale.
Last week the bank offered 5.0 billion shillings in T-bills for sale, of which 4.9352 was sold in competitive rates.
The average weighted prices stood at 97.31, a drop from last week's 97.401. The annualised yield rose to 10.705 from 10.425 last week.
The bank said it would tender 4.0 billion in T-bills next week. Officials said demand was still high but the lower bills on tender was in line with keeping macroeconomic stability.
